entities.summary: Zbyněk Zajíc of Hazmburk or of Hasenburg was a Czech nobleman and an important representative of the Roman Catholic Church in the Crown of Bohemia. He played a crucial role in the governance of the Holy Roman Empire, serving as the Archbishop of Prague from 1403 to 1411. During his tenure, Zbyněk Zajíc oversaw the construction of several important churches and monasteries, including the Prague Cathedral and the monastery of St. George in Olomouc. He also mediated between the Holy Roman Emperor and the Kingdom of Hungary, helping to maintain a fragile peace in the region. Zbyněk Zajíc's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to establish the Czech Lands as a major center of Catholicism in the region. His contributions to the Church and his role in maintaining regional stability have had a lasting impact on the history of the Czech Republic and the wider region.

Zbyněk Zajíc of Hazmburk or of Hasenburg (zbynk-zajc) was a Czech nobleman and a prominent representative of the Roman Catholic Church in the Crown of Bohemia. He played a crucial role in the governance of Bohemia during the late 14th century.

Zbyněk Zajíc was born in 1376 in the Kingdom of Bohemia and died on October 7, 1411. He succeeded Olbram of Škvorec as the 5th Archbishop of Prague in 1403 and served until his death in 1411.

His significance lies in his contributions to the Roman Catholic Church and his influence on the governance of Bohemia. He was a key figure in the Catholic Church's efforts to consolidate power and establish a stable religious authority in the region.




Zbyněk Zajíc's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Roman Catholic Church in Bohemia and its successor states. His role in shaping the religious and political landscape of the region has had a lasting impact on the history of the area.










Zbyněk Zajíc of Hazmburk's significance is rated as 7, reflecting his regional importance and lasting impact on the Catholic Church and Bohemian governance. His contributions to the Church and governance have had a lasting impact on the region, making him a significant figure in the history of Bohemia.
